overall: Tomorrow (Sunday, July 12) in Atlanta is expected to be a warm, unsettled day with a chance of showers and thunderstorms, particularly in the morning and again in the afternoon. The NWS forecasts a high near 90°F, though temperatures may fall back to around 86°F in the afternoon as storm activity increases. Precipitation chances reach 50% during the day and jump to 80% Sunday night, suggesting convective cooling could play a meaningful role in capping the daytime high.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable spread among source models: GFS runs warm at ~91.8°F and HRRR at ~90.3°F, while ECMWF (~87.0°F) and NBM (~86.8°F) are considerably cooler, with GEM (~88.2°F) and Weather.com (~87.9°F) in between. This ~5°F inter-model spread reflects genuine uncertainty around storm timing and coverage — the cooler models likely account for earlier or more widespread convective activity suppressing the afternoon high.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble expected TMAX is 87.3°F, while the forecast-only model sits higher at 90.3°F; the NWS narrative of 'high near 90' with afternoon cooling to ~86°F supports a peak somewhere in the 88–91°F range. The active even-bucket market's top bucket is 90–91°F at 29.4% — a Tier 1 signal with a substantial 15.8-point gap over the next bucket (88–89F at 13.6%), indicating moderate-to-good confidence in that range. Balancing the warm-side NWS/HRRR/GFS guidance against the cooler ECMWF/NBM models and the ensemble mean of 87.3°F, the best single estimate for tomorrow's TMAX is around 89.5°F, with the 90–91°F bucket representing the most likely single outcome if afternoon storms are delayed.
